holidays.name: National Be Late for Something Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek invitation to show up fashionably behind schedule, just once. It's a day to ditch the stopwatch, take the long way, and let the world wait a few minutes for you.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a favorite on quirky-holiday calendars as a playful counterpoint to all the punctuality preached the rest of the year.
holidays.funFact: Many cultures treat arriving a little late to social gatherings as good manners. In some places, showing up exactly on time to a party can mean you're the first guest, and that can be awkward for the host.

holidays.name: National Cheese Pizza Day
holidays.description: A salute to the purest pizza of all: dough, sauce, and a blanket of melty mozzarella with no toppings to distract you. It's the simple slice that has won over kids, purists, and late-night snackers for generations.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It likely grew out of pizza fans' love for the classic cheese pie as the baseline for judging any pizzeria.
holidays.funFact: Many pizza lovers argue that a plain cheese slice is the best test of a pizzeria. With no toppings to hide behind, the crust, sauce, and cheese all have to be good.

holidays.name: World Samosa Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the crispy, golden, spiced-potato-stuffed triangle that fuels tea breaks and street-food adventures. Fans mark it by tucking into samosas with chutney, whether classic potato and peas or creative fillings.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin, popularized by food lovers who wanted a day to honor the beloved snack.
holidays.funFact: The samosa's ancestors are thought to have traveled along trade routes from the Middle East and Central Asia into South Asia centuries ago. There they picked up the potatoes and spices we associate with them today.
